You are painting a poster-style badge that represents a software project plan. It is shown LARGE, at 128px and above (up to 512px), never in a small list slot, so it can carry a full composition. It must still read as one strong silhouette at 128px, and it should be memorable.

Art direction: Poster art: a rich, layered composition with real depth (a background, a middle ground and a foreground), light and shadow built from overlapping shapes, gradients and opacity, a deliberate palette of a few harmonious colors, all held together by ONE strong, instantly readable silhouette. It should be a picture someone remembers after one look.

Paint the plan's SUBJECT as one scene built from vector shapes. Do NOT put letters, words, or a monogram in the picture.

Output requirements (STRICT):
- Output ONLY a single complete <svg>...</svg> element. No markdown fences, no prose, no explanation.
- The root <svg> MUST use viewBox="0 0 100 100" and MUST declare xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg".
- Self-contained: no external references, no <image>, no <script>, no external fonts.
- Use ONLY <g>, <path>, <circle>, <ellipse>, <rect>, <polygon>, <polyline>, <line>, and <linearGradient>/<radialGradient> inside <defs>, with fill-opacity, stroke-opacity or opacity for depth.
- Do NOT use <filter>, <mask>, <clipPath>, <pattern>, <text>, <use>, <style> or CSS; the picture is also rasterized by a renderer that ignores them.
- Fill the whole 100x100 canvas edge to edge; keep the complete SVG under 20 KB.

Plan title: Deep Clones
Plan description: Clone git repos fast so a new agent pod starts working in seconds.
